results.headline: Half Year 2026 Results
results.key_quote: We are pleased to report a significantly improved financial performance in H1 2026 compared to the same period last year. Revenue increased by 32%, supported by improved production quality and stronger prices achieved...these initiatives have materially reduced our cost base.
results.summary: Gem Diamonds reported significantly improved H1 2026 results with revenue up 32% to US$59.7m, underlying EBITDA swinging from negative US$2.6m to positive US$8.6m, and attributable profit of US$0.6m versus prior year loss of US$11.7m. Average price per carat increased 38% to US$1,395. Net debt improved by US$19.6m to US$0.5m. The CEO explicitly stated 'significantly improved financial performance' and 'materially reduced our cost base', indicating results substantially exceeded prior performance. While no explicit analyst/market expectations comparison is stated, the magnitude of improvement and language used demonstrates strong outperformance of prior year baseline and internal guidance.
metrics_ahead: Underlying EBITDA turned positive from negative
Attributable profit swing from loss to profit
Average price per carat +38% to US$1,395

results.headline: Investee Company Update
results.key_quote: Both investments now have the potential to generate significant near-medium term capital release opportunities for Jangada, supplementing the Company's existing cash position in excess of £1 million.
results.summary: Jangada Mines announced positive updates from two investee companies (Fodere and Axies) progressing toward IPOs, which could create capital release opportunities. However, this is an investee company update rather than results announcement with no comparison of Jangada's own operational or financial performance versus expectations. results.headline: AGM Trading Update
results.key_quote: Performance during the 17 weeks to 30 August 2026 remained consistent with the positive trends reported at our FY26 results, leaving us well positioned to deliver on our FY27 guidance.
results.summary: WOSG reports trading momentum consistent with FY26 results with encouraging performance across US and UK markets. Strong demand across luxury brands and strategic growth pillars (Luxury Jewellery, Certified Pre-Owned, Ecommerce). Showroom development programme advancing as planned. Crucially, the company reiterates FY27 guidance without upgrading - maintaining revenue growth of 5-10% at constant currency and 40-80bps EBIT margin expansion. The language emphasizes consistency with previous trends and confidence in achieving guidance, but does not indicate results are ahead of expectations or warrant guidance upgrades.

results.headline: AGM Statement & Intended Move to the Main Market
results.key_quote: our London Gatwick operation continues to perform ahead of our initial expectations, supported by a stronger-than-expected package holiday mix
results.summary: Jet2 reports sustained demand for leisure travel products with booked-to-date passengers up 8.8% year-on-year and booked load factor 1.5ppts ahead of prior year. The London Gatwick operation is performing ahead of initial expectations with a stronger-than-expected package holiday mix, leading to increased aircraft allocation for Summer 2027. Winter 2026/27 shows early booking trends similar to Summer with strong protection via fuel and FX hedging. Results are ahead of stated expectations.
metrics_ahead: London Gatwick operation performance ahead of initial expectations
Package holiday mix stronger than expected
Booked load factor 1.5ppts ahead of prior year

results.headline: Half Year Results
results.key_quote: Good progress in implementing the business improvement plan; improved seasonal H1 trading loss
results.summary: Camellia reported H1 2026 results showing improved trading performance versus the prior year (trading loss improved from £9.6m to £5.0m, EBITDA profit of £19.3m vs loss of £6.2m in H1 2025), driven by cost discipline and favourable pricing/yields. However, the company makes no explicit comparison to market or analyst expectations. Results are presented as showing progress on the Value Enhancement Plan with early contributions expected to build over time. The company acknowledges headwinds from external events (Gulf events, El Niño, Kakuzi profit warning) and states that full-year outcome is 'difficult to predict', with a further update expected in late October. This reflects cautious guidance rather than beating expectations.

results.headline: Trading update
results.key_quote: year-end net debt is now expected to be better than previously indicated and lie in the range of £70 to £90m an improvement of c. £30m
results.summary: Crest Nicholson reports mixed results: debt reduction is significantly ahead of plan with net debt expected to be better than previously indicated (£70-90m vs. prior £100-120m guidance, a £30m improvement). However, profitability guidance has been substantially lowered due to weaker market conditions—full-year EBIT now expected to be a loss of around £10m versus prior guidance of £5m-£10m profit. Completions guidance also reduced to 1,350-1,400 from 1,400-1,500. The positive debt progress is materially ahead, but operational performance is well below expectations.
metrics_ahead: net debt reduction (£30m better than previously guided)
debt reduction progress ahead of plan

results.headline: Hope & Gorob Copper-Gold Project Update
results.key_quote: Development activities at both the Tsoaxaub Metals Processing Plant and the Hope & Gorob mine site continue to progress in line with the current project schedule.
results.summary: Bezant reports that Hope & Gorob copper-gold project development is progressing in line with schedule, with first ROM ore expected to be processed in September 2026. The company has expanded its Phase II review to include previously sub-economic mineralisation based on improved commodity prices, and is evaluating a higher mass-pull ore sorter strategy. Life of mine potential has increased to approximately 35 years. However, no revised economic model has been published, and the company explicitly states it is not yet providing updated financial guidance. Results are tracking to plan rather than beating expectations.

results.headline: Half Year Results and Proposed Open Offer
results.key_quote: The primary driver of the period's bottom-line performance related to net movements in the accounting valuation of Tapir's core holding in Rendeavour.
results.summary: Tapir Holdings reported half-year results for the period ended 30 June 2026 with no explicit comparison to market, analyst, or board expectations. However, the statement notes a net loss was recorded due to non-cash dilution adjustments, though the balance sheet is described as robust. results.headline: Interim Results
results.key_quote: Adjusted PBT from continuing operations of £32.8m, down 5.2% vs H1 2025 but ahead of expectations.
results.summary: Hilton Food Group reported H1 2026 adjusted PBT from continuing operations of £32.8m, which despite being down 5.2% year-on-year, was explicitly stated as ahead of expectations. The company upgraded its full-year adjusted PBT guidance to £66m-£71m (from previous £60m-£65m), reflecting removal of Dalco losses and favourable FX. Core meat and fresh prepared food performed well, though Foppen weakness was a headwind. Strategic progress continues with Dalco sale agreed and new facility launches planned.

results.headline: Half-year Results
results.key_quote: EnQuest enters the second half of 2026 from a position of strength and, looking ahead, 2027 will mark the beginning of a new era for the Group.
results.summary: EnQuest announced half-year results for H1 2026 with production growth and strong operational cash flow. The company announced transformational acquisitions in Malaysia expected to complete 31 December 2026, which would increase production to ~100,000 Boepd (134% increase), reduce unit costs to $16/Boe (35% reduction), and expand reserves significantly. While the CEO discusses a 'position of strength' and 'most exciting and value-creating' years ahead, no explicit comparison is made between reported H1 2026 results and market or analyst expectations. results.headline: 2026 Full-year results
results.key_quote: FY26 was a year of strong progress as we completed a two-year period of transformation, investment and organisational restructuring to Reignite Growth. We returned to positive annual net flows, with growing momentum across the business.
results.summary: Brooks Macdonald delivered ahead of expectations with record FUMA of £21.7bn (14% increase), a significant turnaround to net inflows of £226m (£600m improvement vs FY25), and strong operational momentum. Platform MPS grew 35%, BPS FUM +9%, and Brooks Financial contributed 10% like-for-like revenue growth. Revenue increased 6% to £118.1m and underlying PBT was £29.0m with a 24.6% operating margin. The company has achieved its 21st consecutive year of dividend growth (2.5% increase). All metrics demonstrate the successful completion of their transformation strategy with positive net flows restored after three consecutive years of outflows.
metrics_ahead: Net inflows of £226m (£600m improvement vs prior year)

results.headline: Third Quarter Trading Update
results.key_quote: Projected Adjusted Diluted EPRA EPS for FY 2026 expected to be in the lower half of the range of analyst forecasts
results.summary: Safestore reported Q3 revenue growth of 4.1% at CER, with continued UK and Expansion Market growth. However, the company guided that full year FY 2026 Adjusted Diluted EPRA EPS is expected to be in the lower half of analyst forecast ranges, indicating results are tracking in line with or slightly below market expectations. Like-for-like performance was mixed: UK LFL revenue up 1.9%, Expansion Markets LFL revenue strong at up 11.6%, but Paris LFL revenue down 2.5% due to new store cannibalization and economic headwinds. No guidance upgrade or downgrade was announced, with the company maintaining its position within the forecast range albeit at the lower end.

results.headline: Molaoi Update
results.key_quote: These preliminary results indicate that the Molaoi energy requirement to grind the ore sits well within the standard energy consumption range.

The company reported preliminary comminution test work results showing the ore is 'Medium-Hard' with a DWi of 8.66 kWh/t, which falls well within the standard global range of 6-12 kWh/t for SAG mills. The update includes progress on drilling activities and equipment procurement. However, this is an operational update with no comparison to market expectations, analyst forecasts, or guidance ranges. results.headline: Interim Results

The company returned to profit (£1.9m PBT vs £3.4m loss in H1 2025) and reduced net bank debt by £6.8m. Management provided full-year guidance stating they 'currently expect financial year performance to be marginally ahead of 2025', indicating performance ahead of expectations, though management notes caution due to economic environment and Q4 significance.

results.headline: Financial Results for the Year Ended 31 March 2026
results.key_quote: The Company remains on track to fully complete on time and within budget its restart construction activities by the end of Q1 2027.
results.summary: Tungsten West reported results for the year ended 31 March 2026 showing an operating loss of £7.9 million (improved from £19 million prior year). The company is executing its restart plan for the Hemerdon tungsten and tin mine on track and on budget, with first production already achieved in Q3 2026 and full commissioning expected Q1 2027. Key achievements include £43 million equity raise in February 2026, £25.5 million year-end cash position, and zero lost time incidents. Post-year highlights include £71 million UK Government National Wealth Fund investment announced in August 2026. The company is meeting its operational milestones and timeline but no explicit statement indicates results are ahead of or beating market/analyst expectations.

results.headline: Full Year Financial Results for 2025
results.key_quote: the Group faced increasing external challenges which hindered our ability to operate and generate the socio-economic contributions we provide for our people and Ukraine
results.summary: Ferrexpo reported significantly deteriorated financial performance in 2025. Revenue declined 16% to US$787m, Underlying EBITDA collapsed 60% to US$28m, operating cash flow fell 97% to US$3m, and the company reported a US$224m net loss including a US$154m non-cash impairment. The company was forced to reduce capacity from 50% to 25% due to VAT refund withholding and energy infrastructure attacks, eventually shutting down operations entirely for a period. Management announced the need to raise approximately US$100m in equity capital to continue operations over the next 18 months. All key metrics are materially below prior year performance and indicate significant operational deterioration.
